ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, as amended (AML/CFT Act 2009), ss 5 (definition of beneficial owner: 25% threshold), 31-41 (customer due diligence), 54-61 (politically exposed persons and enhanced due diligence); Companies Act 1993, ss 87-96 (share register and substantial shareholder disclosure); Companies (Information) Rules 2016; AML/CFT Codes of Practice issued by the Financial Markets Authority, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, and Department of Internal Affairs; Sanctions Act 2019 and United Nations Sanctions Regulations for targeted financial sanctions; FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 22 and 24. Note: For the custom 'International Company' classification (ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC), incorporation is effected through the New Zealand Companies Office; no general offshore 'International Company' exemption exists in New Zealand statute, and any tax-exempt characterization (Tax_Exempt_Zone) must be evidenced by a specific statutory instrument or applicable non-resident regime.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory protocols: (1) PEP screening against recognized PEP lists maintained by the AML/CFT supervisor and international databases (World-Check or Dow Jones) for every UBO, director, and authorized signatory; (2) sanctions screening against the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List under the Sanctions Act 2019, the UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN List for all USD-denominated wire transfers and Letter of Credit transactions; (3) adverse media checks for environmental, maritime, and commodity-trading red flags specific to elemental sulfur dry-bulk cargoes; (4) enhanced due diligence for all non-resident UBOs, trust beneficiaries, and companies incorporated in the Cook Islands or other low-tax jurisdictions; (5) documentation of source of funds for initial capitalization (minimum share capital is not statutorily fixed in New Zealand, but bank KYC will typically require not less than USD 1,000 at account opening); (6) continuous monitoring under AML/CFT Act 2009 s 51 in line with FATF Recommendation 10.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (online Companies Register) at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz; the registration and name reservation portal is integrated into the 'Business Connect' online services.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must consist of letters of the English or Māori alphabet or a combination of English and Māori, numerals, and certain symbols; a name in non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese characters) is not accepted unless accompanied by an approved phonetic transliteration in Latin characters; the name must not exceed 100 characters including spaces; for a company limited by shares, the name must end with the word 'Limited', unless the Registrar grants an exemption under Companies Act 1993 s 21(2); the Registrar will reject names that are offensive, misleading, infringing of intellectual property, or that contain restricted words under s 22.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation under Companies Act 1993 s 23 is valid for 20 working days (approximately 30 calendar days). No statutory extension is available; the applicant may file a fresh reservation after the expiry of 5 working days. If the Registrar rejects a name, the applicant receives a written statement of reasons. Procedure: (1) submit a reconsideration request to the Companies Office Name Review team within 15 working days of rejection, together with any consent letters or registrable evidence; (2) if the name remains rejected, file an appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under s 386 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days of the final decision; (3) before filing an appeal, instruct local counsel to prepare an originating application; the Companies Office may also accept a request for an administrative override where a restricted word can be justified (e.g., consent from a sector regulator for the word 'Trust'). Practical remedy: reserve up to three alternate names simultaneously to avoid operational delay; the filing fee per name reservation is NZD 10.00, approximately USD 6.00.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to conditions: the registered office must be a physical New Zealand address (not a PO Box) as required by Companies Act 1993 s 189, capable of accepting legal service and official notices. Virtual offices and registered-agent addresses are accepted by the Companies Office, but a shared mailbox-only address may trigger the Registrar's address-verification program. For a dry-bulk sulfur brokerage entity, a virtual office is acceptable for statutory compliance; however, banks issuing SWIFT letters of credit and charterparty counterparties will commonly require a contractual address, and vessel charterers may require evidence of substantial office presence (e.g., organizational chart, licensed broker arrangements) before contracting. The entity's tax-exempt characterization must be analyzed under the Income Tax Act 2007 to ensure that board and management functions are not exercised in New Zealand in a manner that creates tax residence or a permanent establishment; no employees or operational staff should be located in New Zealand unless the applicable exemption instrument so provides.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk. New Zealand's AML/CFT supervisors (Department of Internal Affairs, Financial Markets Authority, and Reserve Bank) conduct targeted on-site inspections of reporting entities; for a registered-agent address used by a dormant trading vehicle, the annual inspection probability is estimated at 15-20% during the first year and 10% thereafter. The Companies Office also performs routine physical address verification for companies that register a non-PO-Box office; sample inspection risk is estimated at 5-10% per year. If the sulfur trading activity grows to trigger registration as a reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the likelihood of a compliance visit rises to approximately 30% within 18 months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss. 12–20 (incorporation by registration, effects of registration, and certificate of incorporation), s. 122 (registered office), s. 124 (address for service), Schedule 2 (default constitution when no bespoke constitution is filed), and Part 8 (director duties); read with the Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994 and the International Companies (Exempt Status) Regulations 2021 (as adopted for Tax-Exempt Zone International Companies), and, to the extent physical handling of sulfur occurs, the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an operational division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), which administers the New Zealand Companies Register and serves as the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN/1 – Application for Registration of a Company (official electronic incorporation application submitted through the New Zealand Companies Register portal at companysoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit account requirement. The company may be registered with a nominal share capital (e.g., one ordinary share of NZ$1.00). Shares issued for cash or non-cash consideration must be paid in full or credited as paid prior to the issue of share certificates; any allotment for non-cash consideration must satisfy the solvency test under s. 4 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (AN INTERNATIONAL COMPANY) — Adopted on [DATE] at [PLACE] pursuant to ss. 12–20 and s. 122 of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) and the International Companies (Exempt Status) Regulations 2021.

RESOLVED that:
1. The company, being duly incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 as an International Company with Tax-Exempt Zone status (Company Number [NUMBER]) and having its constitution registered, shall carry on the business of dry bulk marine transport and brokerage of granular elemental sulfur (ISIC 4669 / NAICS 423520) and such other lawful activities as the board may from time to time determine.
2. The subscribers to the constitution do hereby take, subscribe for and are allotted [NUMBER] ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each, numbered 1 to [NUMBER], in the name of [SUBSCRIBER NAME], and the directors acknowledge receipt of the total subscription consideration of NZ$[AMOUNT] in cash (or, in the case of non-cash consideration, the board records that the fair value satisfies the solvency test under s. 4 of the Act). The directors are directed to enter the allotment in the share register and to issue share certificates under the company's seal.
3. The registered office of the company shall be situated at [STREET ADDRESS, CITY, NEW ZEALAND], and the address for service of process and documents shall be [ADDRESS OR PO BOX, NEW ZEALAND]. The directors are authorized to file all notices required under ss. 122 and 124 of the Companies Act 1993.
4. [DIRECTOR NAME] is appointed as the sole director of the company, and [SECRETARY NAME] is appointed as company secretary (if applicable), each to hold office until removal, resignation, or vacation of office in accordance with the Act and the constitution. The director(s) shall have full authority to supervise the company's affairs, execute trade contracts, and appoint agents or brokers for the sulfur trading business.
5. The directors are authorized to open, operate and maintain bank account(s) with [BANK NAME] in New Zealand and abroad, and the banking mandate shall be exercised by any one signatory named in the approved mandate card. In particular, the directors are authorized to establish SWIFT payment instructions and documentary Letter of Credit facilities, and to sign treasury and settlement documents for the company's dry bulk commodity transactions.
6. The corporate seal of the company is adopted in the form exhibited; all deeds, contracts, bills of lading, and documents executed by the company shall be signed by two directors, or by one director and the secretary, and, where required, affixed with the corporate seal.
7. The directors are authorized and directed to procure all post-incorporation formalities, including the Inland Revenue registration and Tax-Exempt Zone declaration, hazardous substance location approvals (if incidental storage in New Zealand is carried on), environmental compliance certificates, and all shipping, brokerage, and insurance documentation necessary for the import, export, and brokerage of granular elemental sulfur.

Adopted and signed by the chairperson on [DATE] at [PLACE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online portal: New Zealand Companies Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name (e.g., '[COMPANY NAME] Limited') is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or a reserved name in New Zealand, and that it does not contain a restricted word requiring consent. Submit the application for reservation of name, pay the applicable fee, and obtain the Registrar's reservation for a period of 20 working days. For an International Company, the name must include the words 'Limited' or the suffix 'International Company' to alert third parties to its exempt status.
required_dossiers: Application for reservation of company name
Proposed name with appropriate legal suffix
Brief description of principal business (ISIC 4669 sulfur mineral ore trade)
Contact details of applicant or proposed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or too similar to an existing name, file an alternative name application within the 20-working-day reservation window. If the refusal is based on a restricted or prohibited word, obtain and file the written consent of the relevant regulatory authority, or petition the Registrar under s. 22 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Director Consents, and Registered Office Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and New Zealand Companies Office (for eventual filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company constitution either by adopting the default rules contained in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993 or by filing a bespoke constitution compliant with ss. 24–26 of the Act, including provisions on share capital classes, director powers, indemnification, and dispute resolution. Obtain each proposed director's signed consent to act, duly witnessed, and secure a registered office in New Zealand (a physical street address only; a PO Box is acceptable solely for the address for service).
required_dossiers: Company constitution (bespoke or adoption of Schedule 2)
Consent to Act as Director (Form NZCN/2) for each proposed director
Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address of each director
Registered office letter of consent or landlord permission
Address for service details (physical or PO Box in New Zealand)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the constitution as inconsistent with the Companies Act 1993, correct the offending provisions and refile. If a director consent is stale (executed more than 60 days before filing), obtain a fresh signed consent prior to submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Application and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form NZCN/1 (Application for Registration of a Company) electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register, attaching the constitution (if bespoke) and each director's signed consent. Disclose the registered office, address for service, share structure, and director and shareholder particulars. Pay the prescribed incorporation fee online. Upon compliance with s. 14 of the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which assigns the company number and fixes the date of incorporation. After incorporation, the company must ensure its registers are maintained at the registered office in accordance with s. 189.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN/1 (Application for Registration of a Company)
Company constitution (if bespoke, attach to application)
Consents to Act as Director for all directors
Proposed registered office and address for service
Share structure and subscriber particulars
Payment confirmation of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete particulars, respond to the Registrar's 'Request for Further Information' within 20 working days. If the application lapses or is rejected, refile a corrected application with supporting documents and pay any resubmission fee; administrative correction of minor errors is available under s. 360 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Registered Office and Address for Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical location in New Zealand accessible by the public during business hours and that the address for service is valid for service of legal documents. The registered office details are captured on Form NZCN/1; if changes occur post-incorporation, file Form NZCN/3 (Notice of Change of Registered Office or Address for Service) with the Registrar within 10 working days of the change.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN/1 (registered office section) or Form NZCN/3 (for post-incorporation changes)
Proof of registered office address (lease, title, or landlord consent)
Agent's consent if the address for service is that of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar determines the registered office is not a physical New Zealand address, promptly file Form NZCN/3 with the correct address; late filing penalties may be waived where the error was inadvertent, self-disclosed, and rectified within a reasonable period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Allotment of Shares, Issuance of Certificates, and Establishment of Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Company Secretary (internal corporate action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the first board resolution authorizing the allotment of shares and the issuance of share certificates. Open the statutory registers: share register, register of directors, register of directors' interests, and minutes book, each in accordance with ss. 84–96 and s. 189 of the Companies Act 1993. Record the allotment in the share register, prepare and issue physical or electronic share certificates signed by two directors or one director and the secretary, and ensure the registers are available for inspection where required by law.
required_dossiers: Executed first board resolution
Share certificates (signed and sealed, if applicable)
Share register and register of directors
Subscription agreement or share application forms
Minutes of the board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the allotment is procedurally defective, the board may ratify or rescind the allotment by unanimous resolution and reissue correct certificates; if a certificate is lost or destroyed, issue a replacement upon receipt of a declaration of loss and indemnity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Approval of Trade Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in New Zealand (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) and the New Zealand Companies Office for KYB verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, board resolution authorizing account opening, and certified director identity documents to the chosen bank. Complete the bank's customer due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, declare all beneficial owners, and specify the approved payment rails for the sulfur trade: SWIFT wire transfers and documentary Letters of Credit (export/import LCs). The bank will record the company's AML/CFT risk as a low-risk standard commercial trading entity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Constitution
Certified passports of directors and beneficial owners
Board resolution approving account opening and banking mandate
Business plan and sample trade contracts (for KYC)
Tax-exempt status declaration (Income Tax Act 2007)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide source-of-funds declarations and underlying trade contracts; if the application is declined, apply to another New Zealand licensed bank or a registered non-bank financial institution, or submit a complaint to the Banking Ombudsman Scheme for procedural review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: IRD Registration, Tax-Exempt Status Declaration, and Industrial/Environmental Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) New Zealand; WorkSafe New Zealand; Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the IRD for an IRD number using Form IR742 and simultaneously file the non-resident / Tax-Exempt Zone declaration (Form IR596) to confirm that no New Zealand income tax is chargeable on foreign-source trading income derived by the exempt International Company. Confirm the regulatory scope of the sulfur business: pure brokerage and marine transport of granular elemental sulfur under ISIC 4669 does not require an industrial trading license. If the company will incidentally store, handle, or trans-ship granular sulfur in New Zealand, file the appropriate HSNO registration or location approval application with the EPA, obtain a fire safety certificate from FENZ for the storage premises, and implement the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 obligations administered by WorkSafe New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Form IR742 (Company Details) and Form IR596 (Non-Resident / Exempt Status Declaration)
Certificate of Incorporation
Constitution and board resolution confirming offshore trading scope
Trade contracts evidencing non-resident trading activity
Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for granular elemental sulfur (UN 1350)
HSNO location registration or approval application (if incidental storage)
FENZ fire safety certificate and structural engineer's letter (if warehousing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD contests the exempt status, submit a tax residence certificate from the associated jurisdiction and amend the constitution to restrict New Zealand-source business activities; if the EPA rejects a location approval, invoke the HSNO objection procedure and, if necessary, appeal to the Environment Court; any WorkSafe improvement or prohibition notice must be remedied by a compliance plan and verified by a follow-up inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial operating license is mandated for ISIC 4669 / NAICS 423520 dry bulk marine transport and brokerage of granular elemental sulfur. Should the company undertake physical storage, handling, or trans-shipment in New Zealand, the competent authorities are WorkSafe New Zealand (workplace health and safety) and the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand (hazardous substances registration and compliance under the HSNO Act 1996).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No national wholesale merchant or trading license applies to mineral ore brokerage. Incidental physical activities, if conducted, require a 'Hazardous Substances Location Approval' or a 'Location Registration' under the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Substances Locations) Notice 2017 for Class 4.1 Flammable Solids (UN 1350 granular sulfur), together with a Fire and Emergency New Zealand fire safety certificate for the storage site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, administering the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 (HSNO), in coordination with the relevant regional council administering the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA) for discharge and land-use consents; the Ministry for the Environment (MfE) is the national policy authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Pure brokerage activity: EIA/AEE (Assessment of Environmental Effects) not triggered and the activity is exempt from resource consent. Incidental storage of packaged granular sulfur below the threshold quantities in the HSNO Location Notice: 'Registration Only' tier, requiring electronic registration of the location with the EPA and compliance with prescribed generic controls. Storage at or above the HSNO location threshold for Class 4.1 flammable solids: 'Location Approval' tier, and where the site adjoins a sensitive receiving environment (coastal water, groundwater, residential zone), an AEE under Schedule 4 of the RMA 1991 may be required as part of a land-use resource consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge is permitted from a brokerage operation. For incidental stockpiling, stormwater run-off must be contained on impervious surfaces and treated to meet the receiving-water quality standards of the applicable Regional Plan (typically total suspended solids ≤ 50 mg/L, pH 6–9, no detectable free sulfide, and no visible oil or grease). Air emissions: dust from sulfur handling is subject to the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004 (ambient PM10 standard of 50 µg/m³ as a 24-hour mean); volatile organic compound (VOC) emission limits are not applicable to elemental sulfur. Waste handling: any contaminated material or spent packaging must be classified and disposed of under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Waste) Regulations, with consignment tracking for hazardous waste codes where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ): fire safety certificate issued for any storage premise, including fire load calculation, separation distances for Class 4.1 flammable solids, and approved fire suppression or detection systems for large stockpiles. Structural load inspections: certification by a Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) of floor, racking, and stockpile load capacities prior to heavy storage, together with a civil defense emergency plan for the site. Occupational clearance: compliance with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA), including a written hazard register addressing combustible dust and sulfur handling, certified handler competency under the HSNO Act where thresholds require it, an emergency response and evacuation plan, spill containment and emergency shower/eyewash facilities, and, where required by HSNO regulations, a compliance certificate issued by an EPA-recognized compliance certifier with notification to WorkSafe New Zealand.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) New Zealand (Te Tari Taake); official online portal myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Corporate and non-resident taxpayers use myIR for IRD number applications, GST registrations, return filings, assessments, and refund management.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated International Company (IC) must first determine whether it is carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand or deriving New Zealand-sourced income. If it requires a New Zealand tax identification number, either compulsorily or voluntarily, it must apply to the IRD for a non-individual IRD number using form IR596 (IRD Number Application – Non-Individual), attaching certified incorporation documents, constitutional documents, director and shareholder details, registered office address, and evidence of any New Zealand agent appointment. Where the IC will make taxable supplies in New Zealand or elects to register for GST, it must separately apply through myIR or submit the prescribed GST registration form (form IRD484); an IRD number is a prerequisite for GST registration. A non-resident IC whose activities are confined to offshore export trading and whose central management and control remain outside New Zealand may not be required to register for income tax or GST, but obtaining an IRD number should still be considered to support double tax treaty claims, banking compliance, charter-party documentation, and export zero-rating substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election system. The IC is nonetheless entitled to statutory elections relevant to New Zealand indirect tax and international tax compliance: voluntary registration for GST under section 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; application to treat certain cross-border services as outside the scope of GST; GST grouping election where multiple NZ taxable activities are carried on; branch exemption election under the Income Tax Act 2007 for a non-resident company carrying on business through a New Zealand branch; and qualifying foreign trust election where a foreign trust structure is present. New Zealand's hybrid and branch mismatch rules, enacted under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, are mandatory and contain no elective opt-out; a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity must ensure that any offshore deduction is not the result of a hybrid mismatch involving New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a value-added tax administered by the Inland Revenue Department.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; compulsory registration applies when that threshold is exceeded or is likely to be exceeded. The same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services supplied to New Zealand consumers. Voluntary GST registration is available below the threshold where export zero-rating or input credit recovery is commercially justified.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate exists in New Zealand. GST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices containing the supplier's IRD number, total amount, GST component, and required particulars. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the New Zealand Peppol Authority using PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 standards; invoices need not be pre-cleared or stamped by the IRD, but electronic records must be preserved in an accessible format for seven years and made available on audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported from New Zealand are zero-rated under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of the time of supply and retains acceptable evidence of export. For the IC's dry bulk marine transport and brokerage of granular elemental sulfur, zero-rating applies to a direct export sale where legal title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer, the goods are physically removed from New Zealand, and the export is effected by the supplier or on its behalf. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under section 11A where the recipient is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are not directly connected with New Zealand land or goods; offshore brokerage commission for the sale of sulfur to foreign buyers may therefore qualify for zero-rating if the contractual documentation clearly evidences the non-resident recipient and foreign performance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Declaration (electronic declaration via Trade Single Window, formerly Export Entry form C2)
Original or electronic Bill of Lading issued to order, evidencing despatch from New Zealand to the overseas destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-issued foreign exchange receipt substantiating receipt of export proceeds in New Zealand
Commercial invoice and signed purchase/sale contract identifying the non-resident buyer, Incoterms, and export route
Packing list and weight certificate for bulk granular elemental sulfur cargo
End-use or export certificate where customs control requires classification under HS tariff heading 2503.00 for sulfur
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD and New Zealand Customs Service cross-match export declarations, shipping manifests, GST returns, and banking records to verify export zero-rating claims. If goods are not exported within the statutory 28-day period, the supply becomes taxable at 15% GST and the refund is clawed back, with use-of-money interest accruing from the original return due date. Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating claims may trigger shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care or an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for evasion or an abusive tax position. Criminal prosecution may follow for deliberate evasion, with asset subpoenas, director liability, and disqualification from future GST registration; all export substantiation records must be retained for seven years from the date of supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains unrestricted current account and capital account convertibility. There is no general exchange control legislation, and no Reserve Bank approval is required for inbound or outbound fund transfers, dividend remittances, loan repayment, royalty payments, or trade settlement. Both residents and non-residents may freely hold, purchase, and sell foreign currency. The only practical frictions arise from anti-money laundering/counter-financing of terrorism screening under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, sanctions screening administered by the New Zealand Police and Customs, and withholding tax compliance for outbound payments. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 may restrict foreign investment in sensitive New Zealand land and significant business assets, but it does not restrict ordinary commodity trading operations of an International Company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio in New Zealand. A New Zealand-based International Company trading granular elemental sulfur and mineral ores may retain export proceeds in any currency, in any onshore or offshore bank account, without obligation to convert foreign currency receipts into New Zealand dollars. Statutory reporting is limited to statistical data: goods exported from New Zealand must be reported through the New Zealand Customs Service electronic export entry system, and all bank settlement transactions forming part of New Zealands balance of payments must be classified by the reporting bank using New Zealand Reserve Bank purpose codes. Transfer pricing and general tax rules apply where related parties are involved, but no surrender or repatriation timeline is imposed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Moderate as a supplementary treasury rail, but not as a primary banking solution. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex, and Multinet are not registered as New Zealand banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and therefore cannot offer direct exchange settlement account access, documentary letters of credit, or host-to-host SWIFT service bureaus. They may provide multi-currency payment wallets and money transmission services as non-bank financial service providers, subject to anti-money laundering compliance in their home jurisdiction and, if operating into New Zealand, potential registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008. For a Cook Islands International Company, EMIs are restricted to operational spend and temporary liquidity movements; they cannot replace a Tier-1 New Zealand bank for LC issuance, trade settlement, and escrow services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT regulations do not impose a mandatory physical appearance requirement for corporate account opening, but the majority of Tier-1 New Zealand banks require at least one director or senior officer to attend an in-person or high-definition video interview before activation. Remote-only opening is possible for low-risk local corporates with complete certified documentation, but a Cook Islands International Company structure with non-resident ownership will typically trigger enhanced due diligence and a mandatory video conference or in-branch interview. All shareholders and beneficial owners must provide certified true copies of passports, proof of identity, proof of address, and corporate registers. A physical presence may be required where ultimate beneficial ownership is complex, where a trust or offshore foundation is involved, or where the bank cannot obtain independent electronic verification of identities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company jurisdiction with ultimate beneficial owner located in a high-risk or complex structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified certificate of incorporation of the International Company, constitutional documents, register of directors and shareholders, trust deed and any amendments, registered office certificate from the licensed corporate services provider, a clear corporate structure chart linking each shareholder to a natural person, and a written source-of-wealth memorandum explaining the origin of funds for minimum capital and operational injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholder or nominee director arrangement obscuring control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the executed nominee agreement, the professional fiduciary licence of the nominee provider, beneficial ownership declaration signed by the ultimate natural person, power of attorney if applicable, and bank references from the beneficial owners primary banking institution covering at least five years of tax-compliant activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trade-contract red flags such as politically exposed persons, round-tripping, or unexplained third-party payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Package the complete trade file: master sale and purchase agreements, proforma and final invoices, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, weighbridge certificates, SGS/Cotecna or equivalent inspection reports, letter-of-credit draft terms, insurance certificates, and proof of the underlying shipping route for the granular elemental sulfur and mineral ore cargo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-flow inconsistency between the declared commodity class and bank transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide board resolutions authorising the treasury operation, projected trade volumes and counterparty lists, historical audited financial statements of the International Company, statutory export declarations, tax status letters from the New Zealand Inland Revenue Department, and evidence that no statutory mineral trading licence is required under New Zealand law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound shareholder and intercompany funding must arrive by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through an approved Tier-1 correspondent bank into the New Zealand operational account. The payment narrative must explicitly state the purpose: EQUITY CAPITAL INJECTION or SHAREHOLDER LOAN, with the applicable New Zealand balance-of-payments statistical purpose code used by the receiving bank, such as code 100 for equity capital or code 200 for intercompany loans. Banks will require a board resolution, executed subscription agreement or loan agreement, source-of-funds evidence from the contributor, and confirmation that the Overseas Investment Act 2005 is not triggered. Any inbound transfer in excess of ordinary trade volume will be screened against sanctions lists and the entitys KYC risk profile; therefore all financing documents must be collected before the first transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements will be executed through the following clearing rails: (1) direct SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers for supplier payments working capital, commissions, and freight costs; (2) commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and confirmed through MT710 for structured purchases of granular elemental sulfur; (3) documentary collections using SWIFT MT400 when counterparty credit quality is adequate and LC costs are disproportionate; and (4) domestic New Zealand-dollar legs cleared through the Reserve Bank of New Zealands Exchange Settlement Account System under ISO 20022 messaging. Foreign-currency legs involving USD, EUR, and NZD may be netted through CLS where both counterparties support continuous linked settlement. All outbound disbursements must match the underlying invoice, shipping document, inspection certificate, and letter-of-credit terms to satisfy AML/CFT and sanctions screening.

Non-deliverable forwards for restricted or emerging-market currencies such as CNY, INR, and IDR

Plain-vanilla FX call and put options used strictly for hedging confirmed sulphur and mineral ore trade exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing month is the month of the anniversary of incorporation; the return must be filed online on or before the last calendar day of that month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late fee; the Registrar issues a reminder, then a formal notice of intended removal under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993. Failure to remedy within the notice period (normally 20 working days) triggers administrative strike-off, dissolution by Gazette notice, and vesting of remaining assets in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4), including nil return where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date: due 7 July for direct filing, or 31 March of the following year with an approved tax agent extension; provisional tax instalments due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May. A tax-exempt IC with no New Zealand-source income is outside the IR4 filing population.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty (initial NZD 500 for companies) plus late payment interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994; continued default leads to default assessment, enforced collections, and potential director personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Return on six-monthly filing cycle, if GST registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six-monthly taxable periods ending 30 September and 31 March for a 31 March balance date; returns due on the 28th day of the month following each period, namely 28 October and 28 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty, incremental penalties, and late payment interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994; sustained default triggers IR enforcement and recovery action and may result in cancellation of GST registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Auditor's Report (mandatory only for 'large' and 'overseas' companies under the Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If applicable, file within 20 working days of receiving the auditor's report, or 5 months after balance date if the report is not received, whichever is earlier; small and tax-exempt ICs are exempt from filing and statutory audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification notices and court orders compelling filing; directors may face pecuniary penalty orders; ongoing default is a compliance trigger supporting removal from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit is mandatory only if the company is 'large' under section 45 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013: total consolidated assets exceeding NZD 60 million and consolidated revenue exceeding NZD 30 million in each of the last two accounting periods; or if the company is an overseas company or an FMC reporting entity. All other companies ('small' and 'micro') are exempt from audit unless shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights pass a resolution requiring an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS for large for-profit entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) or the XRB Simplified Reporting Framework for small companies with no public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand imposes no standalone annual UBO register filing for the current compliance cycle; however, the annual return must confirm the ultimate holding company and controlling shareholder. All share allotments and transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members within 10 working days, and the register must be reconciled and updated before the annual return is certified. AML/CFT-regulated counterparties require refreshed beneficial ownership confirmation upon any material shareholding change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 185 to USD 430 (NZD 300 to NZD 700) per annum for a registered office address and professional company agent services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 15,000 per annum for a full statutory audit of a mid-sized New Zealand trading company; not normally incurred for a small or tax-exempt IC relying on the statutory audit exemption.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% flat corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act 2007, s RB 3)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit of 15% for eligible research and development expenditure; imputation credit system providing shareholder tax credits on fully imputed dividends. For a CK_IC International Company with non-resident ownership, no New Zealand permanent establishment, and no New Zealand-source income, the effective New Zealand corporate tax rate is 0% (outside the New Zealand tax net).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR portal (or via an approved tax agent using IRD-compatible software).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due 7 July of the same calendar year. For a non-standard balance date, the due date is the 7th day of the 7th month following the balance date. Non-resident companies carrying on a taxable activity through a fixed establishment in New Zealand must also file an IR4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from sales of granular elemental sulfur and marine dry-bulk transport/brokerage services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income from a New Zealand source or attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment; offshore sales receivable booked overseas are excluded unless the economic substance is in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest received, gross of resident withholding tax (RWT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are not liable on interest from foreign-source loans; bank interest from New Zealand banks is usually subject to RWT at 2% or 15% if an RWT-exemption certificate is held.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable dividends from resident and non-resident companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends from a New Zealand company to a non-resident are exempt in the shareholder's hands only to the extent fully imputed; otherwise NRWT applies at the payer level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Demurrage, freight, foreign exchange gains, commissions and any other assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report fair value of New Zealand-source assessable income only; positions inconsistent with the OECD model may trigger CFC rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Purchases / cost of goods sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Acquisition cost of sulfur mineral ore and related freight-in, including LC and demurrage costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must satisfy arm's length pricing under transfer pricing rules; related-party purchases from a tax-exempt supplier must be supported by a transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting all allowable expenses and before tax offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a New Zealand permanent establishment exists, compute net profit using the separate-entity approach and attribute capital to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax credits, foreign income tax credits, and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only for foreign income subject to New Zealand tax; treaty credits must be claimed with a TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance of income tax payable or refundable after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with no NZ-source income should show zero; a refund may arise from RWT over-withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 (paper) or NZ$50 (electronic) under s 139AB, with automatic escalation penalties; strict-liability offence of failure to file under s 143A (up to NZ$1,000 fine). Late payment penalties: 1% on the day after due date, additional 4% after 7 days, then 1% per month thereafter; use-of-money interest (UOMI) runs daily on unpaid tax.
